subject: Clarifying VPC data escrow, retention windows, and deletion attestations
body:
Message 1 — 2026-11-29T16:22:00Z
From: Jordan Price <security@helioshealth.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Cc: Helios Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Subject: VPC deployment — escrow, retention, and deletion Qs

Hi Mina,

Quick set of questions as we scope the private VPC deployment for Helios:

1) Data escrow — does Redwood offer a formal data escrow option for VPC customers (encrypted snapshot deposit to a third-party escrow or S3?) if our legal requires a copy in escrow for continuity? If so, what are the controls and access processes?

2) Residency enforcement — in a private deployment can Redwood guarantee that customer-controlled storage and snapshots remain within a single cloud region (no cross-region backups) and provide a written statement?

3) Deletion / evidence — we need an auditable deletion workflow for tenant data (including backups/snapshots). Can you describe: retention windows for automatic snapshots, how permanent deletes are performed, and what attestation/evidence Redwood can provide (logs, signed receipt, or deleted-file manifest)?

4) KMS / keys — can Helios bring its own KMS for disk/snapshot encryption, and will Redwood operate with customer-managed keys so Redwood staff cannot access plaintext?

5) Time to completion — if we request tenant data purge (end-of-contract), what are typical timelines (including backup sweep) and SLA exceptions?

Appreciate concrete detail (short bullets are fine). We may need this for procurement and legal.

Thanks,
Jordan
Security Lead
Helios Health

Message 2 — 2026-11-30T09:14:00Z
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <security@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Helios Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Subject: RE: VPC deployment — escrow, retention, and deletion Qs

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers and next steps; attaching a short SOC2 summary and a VPC data-flow diagram. I also attached our tenant erase runbook for your review.

1) Data escrow:
- We do not push an escrow copy by default for private VPCs. However, for enterprise contracts we can arrange an escrow workflow: encrypted snapshots (customer-wrapped keys) are exported to a dedicated S3 bucket owned by the customer or to a mutually agreed escrow provider.
- Access model: exports are encrypted with the tenant key (customer KMS recommended). Redwood can automate snapshot export on schedule or on-demand. Redwood only uploads encrypted blobs; the customer or escrow provider controls decryption.
- Process: export request -> snapshot export job -> MD5/sha256 checksums logged -> upload to target bucket -> signed export receipt (timestamped) returned by Redwood.

2) Residency enforcement:
- For private VPCs deployed in a customer cloud region we enforce single-region placement by default. No cross-region replication or backups occur unless explicitly enabled in the contract.
- We will provide a written region-lock statement (in the SOW) identifying the cloud provider and region (e.g., us-west-2).

3) Deletion & evidence:
- Snapshot lifecycle: automatic hourly snapshots retained for up to 48 hours by the serving runtime for fast recovery, with daily snapshots retained for up to 14 days (default), configurable per-customer during onboarding.
- Permanent deletion steps: 1) mark tenant for purge; 2) delete live objects; 3) schedule snapshot purge job that deletes snapshots and exported blobs; 4) overwrite temporary cache and scrub KV caches; 5) run a verification sweep.
- Evidence / attestation: Redwood can provide a deletion report including a job run id, timestamps, list of object keys deleted, checksums where applicable, and an operator-signed attestation PDF. Audit logs (immutable) will show deletion operations and job traces.

4) KMS / keys:
- Yes, customer-managed keys supported. We integrate with major cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and HSM-backed KMS via customer gateways.
- With customer KMS: Redwood never stores tenant master keys; snapshots are encrypted with a key-wrapping key controlled by Helios. Operational staff need an emergency access process (optional) that is gated by written approvals/can be disabled.

5) Purge timelines:
- Typical timeline: 72–120 hours for primary object deletion + snapshot sweep (depends on dataset size).
- If escrow exports exist, final purge is contingent on whether customer requests exported copy removed from escrow.
- SLA exceptions: legal hold, active investigations, or export to escrow requested by customer will extend timelines and be documented in SOW.

Next steps: I recommend a short call to confirm region and KMS model and to add escrow/export language to the SOW. Aditya, can you schedule a 30-min call this week with Jordan? Lauren — FYI on the attestation deliverable.

Best,

Mina Haddad
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com

• For the escrow export receipt: can Redwood include a signed manifest that lists object keys + SHA256 for each exported blob? Our legal needs checksums to validate integrity.
• For the immutable audit logs you mentioned — are those retained by Redwood in our project (tenant) logs or do we need to export them to our logging (we have a central Splunk instance)?

Message 4 — 2026-12-02T11:07:00Z
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Price <security@helioshealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Helios Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Subject: RE: VPC deployment — escrow, retention, and deletion Qs

Jordan — quick answers to your follow-ups (bullets):

• Escrow manifest: yes — we can provide a signed manifest with object keys, sizes, and SHA256 checksums for every exported blob. The manifest is signed with an internal operator signature and timestamped. We include MD5/SHA256 as part of the export job logs.

• Audit logs: Redwood retains immutable service-level audit logs for control plane and data-plane operations for the period in the contract (we default to 90 days). For customers that want longer retention, we offer export hooks to push audit records to the customer’s logging bucket or event stream (CloudWatch/EventBridge, Pub/Sub) — recommended for central Splunk ingestion.

• Immediate wipe SLA: best-case (small dataset, no legal hold, no escrow) — 24–48 hours. Worst-case (large dataset + snapshot purge across many attached volumes) — up to 5 business days. We'll document the exact SLA in the SOW and include any extensions for escrow or legal holds.

Action items:
- Aditya will schedule the call to confirm region and KMS choices.
- Mina to include sample signed export manifest and attestation template in the shared Drive (link attached).
- Procurement to confirm whether Helios will require escrow as a contract condition.

I'll drop the sample manifest and attestation into the folder now.

Thanks — Mina
